trust_decision.summary: The Redis honeypot accepts unauthenticated network input of unbounded size: it buffers, sizes and holds connections without limits. The decision about how much client-declared length, buffered data, idle time and concurrency to accept is made in RedisProtocol (dataReceived and the RESP/inline parsers) and in the CanaryRedis factory settings.

landing_point.why: The summary names the Redis service. dataReceived is the single network entry and appends every packet to self._data without a cap (redis.py:413-416).

fix_sites.entry_point: TCP data on the redis.port listener (default 6379), RedisProtocol.dataReceived
TCP data not starting with '*' (inline command) -> _parseInlineCommand
TCP connect on redis.port (factory; the fix adds timeout and max_connections, fix.diff:747-767)
Operator config file loaded by Config / is_valid (new redis.* range checks, fix.diff:59-102)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No out-of-scope site exists. The only argument a solver could make is that config.py validation is 'operator input, not attacker input', so a negative or boolean redis.max_* value that disables the limits can be left unvalidated.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Commands split across several TCP packets must be buffered and resumed (RedisCommandAgain), and several pipelined commands in one packet must each get a response. A fix that caps the whole connection buffer, or that closes on incomplete frames, breaks both. Setting timeout=0 or max_connections=0 to disable the limit must also keep working (fix.diff:764-767, fix.diff:753-754).

O6_input_shapes: RESP multibulk with a huge declared element count (*N)
RESP bulk string with a huge declared length ($N), including long-digit or leading-zero lengths (fix.diff:798-816)
bulk header or line with no CRLF terminator that grows forever (fix.diff:897-901, fix.diff:937-941)
inline command line with no newline (fix.diff:839-848)
many small fragments accumulating across packets (fix.diff:1205-1210)
pipelined commands, where the limit applies per command (fix.diff:921-922, fix.diff:950-951)
idle or slow connections (TimeoutMixin, fix.diff:764-767, fix.diff:789-796)
non-UTF-8 bytes, so the buffer becomes bytes instead of decode() (fix.diff:1214, fix.diff:1223)

O7_producer.where: opencanary/config.py:120-161 (is_valid has no redis.* checks at the pinned commit) and opencanary/modules/redis.py:443

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second bulk-type parser, such as a RESP3 or other length-prefixed type handled next to '$', that reads its length with int() and no cap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer extending protocol fidelity (the fix already mimics redis 6.0.20 replies) could add another type branch that copies the pre-fix length handling. It is WHERE-type, so it counts only as an extra.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a config value read as a string or float, for example int("0") or a negative number, that silently disables the cap because the factory coerces it without validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The factory reads limits via config.getVal with defaults, and the validation lives in a separate file (config.py:120). A mismatch between the two is a plausible HOW-type sibling.

O9_family: CWE-770 allocation of resources without limits (unbounded buffer, declared length, connection count and idle time in a network protocol parser)

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 with pyproject.toml/uv.lock, Twisted, pytest; the existing tests use the redis client (pyproject.toml:52)
O10_build.project_tests: opencanary/test/test_redis.py at the pinned commit holds integration tests against a running opencanary on localhost:6379 (test_redis.py:7-21). The fix's tests use Twisted StringTransport/Clock unit fixtures (fix.diff:1275-1282).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add one total-size cap on self._data in dataReceived, and miss the declared-length checks, the per-command limit, the idle timeout and the connection limit.

out_of_scope_notes: Other honeypot modules also buffer unbounded input in dataReceived (opencanary/modules/mysql.py:136, opencanary/modules/mssql.py:424, opencanary/modules/mongodb.py:170, opencanary/modules/example1.py:44). These are other services, not this advisory's sink, and were not pursued.

Telnet and git already have max_connections/timeout limits (opencanary/modules/telnet.py:125-140, opencanary/config.py:143-161). They show this project-wide hardening series; the git one is commit 13b0980.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured. The source tree looks small (it may meet tiny_repo, under 5 MB), but this is unconfirmed, so the flag is not set.

At the pinned commit, ProtocolError and ArgumentCountError call bytes.format (opencanary/modules/redis.py:12, opencanary/modules/redis.py:17), which raises AttributeError on Python 3. Error paths may therefore crash rather than close cleanly, which could affect hidden-test design. Not run.
Advisory text itself was not available; the trust decision is drawn from the summary and the diff.
Lessons note resource-exhaustion tasks produced 0 of 7 hard tasks; fit judged 'none' partly on that basis.
